scope: Conditional numerical fields for the newly refitted bilinear source coefficients. No observed motion data are opened or scored.
source_reason: Image and field representations now agree, but source covariance, native pixel/beam treatment, absolute photometry, independent depth constraints, missing phases and physical exterior fields remain incomplete.
source_discretization: The exact same nonnegative bilinear planar nodes used in the image projection, times the declared continuous exponential layers. Integer-factor planar interpolation preserves node-basis integrals; vertical cells use exact exponential cell averages without tail renormalization.
independent_benchmarks: Dense full-volume versus disk-backed Poisson and QUMOND face-flux reference
Independent physical line-of-sight integration of the bilinear source basis
Thin-limit finite-cell integration, flux/centroid, projection adjoint, and held-source mutation controls
Existing Plummer, external-field and cube/covariance analytic controls
limitations: The two stellar models differ in recovered planar structure as well as depth. Their difference is joint deprojection sensitivity, not a pure height effect.
Each resolution and box perturbation is compared with the same base grid. Joint-refinement cross terms are not bounded by these one-at-a-time checks.
Changing the box checks the numerical use of the conditional isolated boundary; it does not measure the environment or validate isolation.
The earlier coefficient set's convergence cannot be inherited. Both new cases must pass their own tests.
Force-equivalent speeds are field diagnostics, not actual orbit solutions in a barred potential.
